lines.text: Thomas Edison sent Hidden to find platinum for light bulb filaments.
He never found platinum, yet the search turned up a green gem.
Kentucky chemist Lawrence Smith named it hiddenite in 1881.

post.caption: Hiddenite honors a man named Hidden. Thomas Edison sent Hidden to find platinum for light bulb filaments. He never found platinum, yet the search turned up a green gem. Kentucky chemist Lawrence Smith named it hiddenite in 1881. The North Carolina community was later renamed Hiddenite. Emeralds came out of that same ground. Hiddenite is green spodumene, colored by chromium. Turn a hiddenite and its green looks lighter or deeper. Pink kunzite is the same mineral, colored by manganese. It has perfect cleavage, so a hard knock can chip it. Visitors can dig for gems at a mine in Hiddenite, North Carolina.
